rotation_note: Unattended-run override: NO rotating subset. All 3 core keywords plus the entire politics pool (34 keywords, grouped into policy_regulation / elections_public_opinion / geopolitics) are working keywords today (37 total). Day-of-year 314 sets ORDER only: group lead rotates so no group leads twice in a row (elections_public_opinion led 11-08, geopolitics led 11-09, so policy_regulation leads today, then elections_public_opinion, then geopolitics); within each group the list starts at offset 314 % group_size in pool order (policy 15 -> 14: 개인정보 AI first; elections 9 -> 8: AI 허위정보 first; geopolitics 10 -> 4: compute diplomacy first). Queries were not checked with WebSearch (budget reserved for librarians); librarians should prefer outlet RSS/sitemap_news feeds over site: search for recency. Window: last brief was 2026-11-09, so items published 11-09 (after the prior harvest) through 11-10 are in scope. Context: Tuesday in Korea / Monday in the US and EU, so weight US Monday agency releases and court dockets (BIS, FTC, FCC, DOJ, federal district courts), EU Monday/Tuesday Commission and Council documents ahead of the informal European Council in Dublin on AI (2026-11-13), Korean Tuesday 국무회의 and 국회 예산 심사 items (과기정통부, 개인정보위, 선관위, 문체부), and Asia-Pacific releases (Japan, India, Singapore, Australia). Upcoming hooks (only official documents are new, previews are not): Dublin informal European Council on AI 11-13 (a draft declaration text or formal Council document is new); CCW 7th Review Conference on autonomous weapons in Geneva 11-16..20 (11-09 card covered the Russia/US blocking push; only a conference decision, formal state working paper, or adopted mandate is new); House closed briefing with Nvidia's Jensen Huang 11-18; lame-duck Congress returns mid-November (NDAA AI provisions, chip-security bills); Meta's AI-scraping commercial terms take effect 11-20 (Norway and Brazil courts suspended them; UK CMA probe open); Delhi HC Kriti Sanon hearing 12-10. In scope: bills introduced/marked up, agency rules/bulletins, court rulings and filings, regulator enforcement, export-control actions, official post-election after-action reports on AI-enabled interference, platform takedown reports. OUT of scope: who won, seat counts, polling, horse-race analysis, commentary without a new document. Neutrality rule from sources.json applies: report decisions/filings/releases, attribute contested claims, no partisan framing.
